source: NCERT Class XII, Contemporary World Politics, Ch. 4 (Alternative Centres of Power).

sections.heading: 1. Emergence of New Power Centres
points: After US hegemony, new **alternative centres of power** rose to balance/challenge it — the **European Union (EU)** and organisations in **Asia (ASEAN, China)**.
These represent a move toward a more **multipolar** world.

sections.heading: 2. The European Union (EU)
points: The **EU** evolved from post-war economic cooperation (European Economic Community) — the **Maastricht Treaty (1992)** created the EU.
It has a **common market, common currency (the Euro), a flag, anthem, and parliament**.
The EU is an **economic, political and diplomatic giant** (a major trade power), but member states retain sovereignty (limits to a common foreign policy).
Some members (e.g. UK) stayed out of the Euro; Britain later left (Brexit).

sections.heading: 3. ASEAN
points: The **Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)** was formed in **1967 (Bangkok Declaration)** by 5 countries (now 10).
It promotes **economic growth, regional peace and cooperation**; the **ASEAN Way** (informal, consultative, non-interference).
It built an **ASEAN Free Trade Area** and community (economic, security, socio-cultural); India has a 'Look East/Act East' policy toward ASEAN.

sections.heading: 4. The Rise of China
points: **China's economic rise** — from **Deng Xiaoping's reforms (1978)** (open-door policy, special economic zones), keeping political (communist) control.
China became the **world's factory** and a major economic power (second-largest economy).
Its growth challenges US dominance; India and China have both cooperation and border tensions.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Alternative power centres: EU and Asia (ASEAN, China).
EU created by the Maastricht Treaty (1992); common currency = Euro.
ASEAN formed 1967 (Bangkok Declaration); 'ASEAN Way' (consensus, non-interference).
China reformed from 1978 (Deng Xiaoping); became the 'world's factory'.
Trend: from unipolar → multipolar world.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Maastricht Treaty (1992)** established the **European Union**; the **Euro** is its currency.
**ASEAN was formed in 1967** (Bangkok Declaration).
**China's reforms began in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping** (open-door policy).
The **EU/ASEAN represent moves toward a multipolar world**.
